A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research on activation functions, gradient-feature separation and NTK conditioning. The complete documents, including figures, equations and appendices, are readable and support comparison despite retitling and reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original measurements of gradient angles and NTK conditioning on five datasets, plus training-loss experiments on MNIST, FashionMNIST and Librispeech.

after.justification: v2 retains those experiments and adds numerical studies of other activations and initialization scales, together with MNIST test accuracies at different depths.

M1.justification: Equation (1) broadens the studied network from fixed ReLU to a general activation with activation-dependent normalization. v2 evaluates ReLU², GeLU and tanh variants. The ReLU architecture and training procedure used in the retained experiments remain unchanged.

E1.justification: Both versions use synthetic Gaussian data, MNIST, FashionMNIST, SVHN and Librispeech. The added activation and initialization studies vary model settings; the new MNIST test-accuracy analysis retains the existing classification task and population.

E2.justification: The corresponding experiments retain linear networks, linear models or the equivalent input-angle reference as comparators. The additional nonlinear activations are subjects of supplementary analyses, rather than new competing baselines evaluated against the proposed ReLU setting.

E3.justification: The original widths, training budgets, optimizer and learning-rate search are retained. Added protocols examine alternative activations at depths 1, 3, 10 and 100, initialization variances 0.01, 0.1, 1 and 10, and MNIST test accuracy after convergence at depths extending to 12.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial analyses of whether separation generalizes across activation functions (Figure 2), survives changes in initialization scale (Appendix B, Figure 6), and accompanies deteriorating generalization at greater depth (Table 1). These extend the original depth analyses to robustness and optimization-generalization questions.

E5.justification: Both versions report averages over five independent initialization seeds for the retained angle and conditioning experiments. v2 introduces no new empirical confidence intervals, significance tests or uncertainty-estimation practice for its additional results.

E6.justification: New Figures 2 and 6 report separation results across activations and initialization scales. Table 1 adds MNIST test accuracies, including 97.57% at depth 6 and 97.19% at depth 12. The original conditioning and training-loss curves are retained as Figures 3 and 4, so these additions do not represent improved scores in repeated original experiments.

T1.justification: v2 adds finite-width probabilistic separation guarantees, an arbitrary-depth conditioning claim with only the first layer trainable, and new infinite-depth theorems and proofs. The latter replace v1's speculative orthogonality and condition-number-one interpretation with angle arccos(1/4) and a stated condition number of (n+4)/3. The earlier two-sample, all-layer conditioning result is retained in Appendix F.

C1.justification: The headline contributions broaden from ReLU to nonlinear activations generally, with new claims about finite-width separation and universal separation in the infinite-width-then-depth limit. The optimization implication is also qualified more explicitly as an improvement in worst-case convergence rates.

C2.justification: v2 adds an optimization-generalization trade-off: increasingly uniform gradient-feature separation can erase input similarity and harm prediction on unseen data. It also supplies a binary-gating explanation for conditioning, explicitly discusses the bias-free applicability boundary, and replaces v1's orthogonality interpretation of infinite depth with a nonorthogonal fixed-angle interpretation.

D1.justification: Section 4.1 newly discloses that each NTK computation used an A100 GPU and took approximately 4–10 hours. Figure 2 also supplies normalization constants for the added activation variants. These disclosures supplement the retained implementation information.

R1.justification: The related-work discussion substantially expands comparisons with prior NTK eigenvalue, spectral and depth-conditioning analyses, including newly cited work by Nguyen, Murray and Xiao and their coauthors. It replaces the broad ReLU survey with explicit positioning around activation-on/off comparisons at finite depth without data-distribution assumptions.

P1.justification: v2 retitles the paper and substantially revises the abstract, introduction, related work and conclusion. It folds the linear-network section into the preliminaries, moves embedding results into the appendices, relocates the two-sample theorem to Appendix F, and reorganizes the exposition around gradient features.

P2.justification: v2 adds a three-panel activation figure, a four-panel initialization-scale figure and the first results table. Figure 1 is redrawn with revised styling and labels, while the original benchmark, training and auxiliary-function figures are retained and renumbered, with some caption and panel-format changes.

improvement.justification: Compared with v1, v2 provides broader numerical evidence, useful generalization qualifications and clearer research positioning. However, its expanded central theory has internal inconsistencies: Appendix E.6's matrix 3I/4 + J/4 implies condition number (n+3)/3, rather than the claimed (n+4)/3. Corollary 3.3 also states L = Omega(1/theta_in), whereas the supporting Appendix G.7 requires theta_in = o(1/L). These issues affect the new guarantees, leaving the net quality change uncertain despite the beneficial additions.
